title: The canon's self-description as religion of religions
statement: The canon presents itself as an atheist, non-supernatural religion and as the demystified common source-tradition of existing religions — the religion of religions — naming Buddhism, Islam, Mormonism, and others as traditions that testify in their own ways to the same creators; this record carries the self-description as explicit source content, against which the incompatible external classifications (four governments, four headings; the scholars' stacked labels) are registered as reception history.

includes: The self-description as the source states it: no supernatural God, mortal plural creators, the message as demystification, the traditions enumerated as testifying (TBWTT-5:54 among the anchors)
The reception-history layer: the documented incompatible classifications by governments and scholarship, carried as fact about reception
The function of this record: when corpus prose calls Raelism an atheist religion or the religion of religions, it is quoting the source's self-understanding, and this record is the citation
excludes: The adequacy of the self-description as a scholarly category, which the Religion of Religions Explainer argues at its own inferred grade
Any claim that the enumerated traditions accept the source's account of them; the comparative work lives in the claims that do it (0007, 0011, 0021, 0024)
Classification disputes' resolution; the record registers them

source_references.locator: TBWTT-1:53 ('We are men like you'); TBWTT-5:54 (the traditions enumerated); TBWTT-5:66 and the closing self-framing the Explainer assembles
The UFO-religion category literature the reception layer registers

alternatives.statement: The incompatible classifications show the self-description does not stabilize a category; 'atheist religion' names a tension, not a genus.
The religion-of-religions framing is a legitimation strategy typical of new religious movements claiming seniority over older traditions.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0020 is revised in a way that affects the source basis.
The canon's fuller context materially changes the self-description.
Public prose begins citing this record for the adequacy of the category rather than for the self-description, which is the record's one forbidden use.
